findings.issue: Pure, easily-testable helpers (humanize, padDex, idFromUrl, latestEnglishFlavor, englishShortEffect, displayValue) have zero tests despite encoding subtle spec rules (last English entry, whitespace collapse, em-dash for missing values).
findings.suggestion: Add a vitest spec for format.ts covering mr-mime, #0025 padding, trailing-slash URL ids, mixed-case/\n/\f flavor text, and null power → '—'.

findings.issue: Filter/pagination/URL-state logic is untested: combined filters, page clamping, page=1 param omission, and reset-to-page-1 on filter change.
findings.suggestion: Test parseQuery and the filtered/currentPage/pageItems computeds against a small fixture catalog: verify q+type+generation intersection, out-of-range page clamps to totalPages, and empty filters produce 1025-equivalent results.

findings.issue: Move-table construction and sorting (nulls sort last in both directions, per-method independent sort state, method priority Level Up > Machine > Egg > Tutor) is entirely untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test compareRows/sortRows and buildTables with mixed null power/accuracy rows and multiple methods; assert ascending vs descending null placement and table ordering.

findings.issue: Failed HTTP requests are cached forever: the errored observable is stored in the cache behind shareReplay({refCount:false}), so a transient error makes a resource permanently resolve to null (Not found) for the session.
findings.suggestion: Remove a failed key from the cache (e.g. via a catchError/tap that deletes cache.get(key)) and add a test that a failed get can succeed on retry.

findings.issue: When a type lists a Pokémon whose id is missing from speciesById, the card label falls back to the raw API URL (entry.url), unlike move-page.ts:66-76 and ability-page.ts:60-74 which drop such entries — a latent rendering bug nothing would catch.
findings.suggestion: Match move/ability pages: filter out entries with no resolvable species name, and add a shared tested helper for the alternate-form/dedup/species-resolution pattern used in three copy-pasted places.

findings.issue: Catalog cross-referencing (id>10000 exclusion, type-slot ordering, generationBySpeciesId) is untested; a refactor that flips the exclusion boundary or loses slot ordering breaks the home page and type badges silently.
findings.suggestion: Test catalog$ construction against fixture data including an alternate form (id 10001) and a multi-slot dual type, asserting exclusion and slot order.

findings.issue: Recursive evolution-tree template (branching chains like Eevee) is untested; a cycle or malformed chain in the data would render incorrectly or blow the stack with no guard.
findings.suggestion: Add a component test rendering a branching chain (Eevee fixture) asserting all 9 species links appear nested correctly.

findings.issue: Sprite fallback uses a per-instance triedFallback flag that is never reset when inputs change (reused card in @for), and the fallback swap is untested.
findings.suggestion: Reset triedFallback in an effect on pokemonId changes, or derive fallback via computed; test that an image error triggers the front_default fallback.

findings.issue: The hand-rolled static server (API_BASE_URL injection, path-traversal guard, SPA fallback) is the production entry point and has no tests.
findings.suggestion: A few node-side vitest cases: injected script present in served index.html, /pokemon/missingno returns the SPA shell, traversal attempts rejected.

findings.issue: Query parsing uses a `params as unknown as Map<string,string>` cast instead of a typed adapter, and parseQuery's NaN/out-of-range handling is untested.
findings.suggestion: Type it honestly against ParamMap and unit-test parseQuery with page=abc, page=0, page=99, and missing params.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own, even though the CLI fully scaffolded vitest (builder, tsconfig, devDeps) and `ng test` is wired. Meanwhile the riskiest logic — filtering, pagination, move-table sorting, catalog cross-referencing, and an HTTP cache with a real error-caching bug — sits completely unguarded. Once the acceptance suite stops being the only safety net, any refactor or data-shape change can break the home page, type pages, or Pokémon pages without a single failing test.
